channel.title: Vista
channel.description: Updates for Vista — eye and movement breaks for the Mac, from Coursion.

item.title: Version 0.2.3
item.description:
2026-10-26

  • Muted meetings stay meetings — Google Meet, Slack huddles and other calls in a browser or app count as a call for as long as that app keeps the call going, even with your microphone muted and camera off. Breaks wait until it ends.
  • Browsers recognised properly — A browser's audio and microphone helpers now count as the browser itself, so a call in Dia, Chrome or Arc is seen as one app.
  • Vista's own mark in the menu bar — The sun over the hills, instead of a camera icon during calls.

item.title: Version 0.2.2
item.description:
2026-10-21

  • Fixed: Vista would not open — 0.2.0 and 0.2.1 were signed with the wrong provisioning profile, so macOS refused to start them. This build opens, keeps iCloud sync, and updates itself from here on.

item.title: Version 0.2.1
item.description:
2026-10-19

  • Move breaks, drawn like the eye breaks — Light, rings and lines in the break's colour show the motion instead of a figure: a point that rises and walks out and back, shoulders that roll, a knee that folds, a ring that tips ear to shoulder, a glass that fills and empties.
  • Neck steps that match the advice — Ear to each shoulder, then chin gently back, not down.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
2026-10-18

  • Breaks that actually happen — A still keyboard is no longer mistaken for time away. Reading, a video or a quiet call keeps the rhythm going; locking the screen or stepping away for five minutes still counts.
  • Any day, any hour — No schedule by default, so the rhythm runs whenever you are at the Mac. Set working hours if you want weekends off.
  • Something to follow — Every exercise has its own scene: the horizon, a blinking eye, palming, near and far, breathing rings, footsteps, shoulder rolls, hip hinges, neck stretches, a glass of water.
  • A countdown you can feel — A glowing ring with a minute dial, digits that roll, and tips that stay long enough to read.
  • Today and Insights — The dashboard joins the settings window: two rhythm rings, the day as a timeline, and what Vista sees right now.
  • Smart pause — A break waits through calls, busy calendar events, a Focus with Vista's filter on, deep-focus apps, full-screen apps and games, video, and the sentence you are in the middle of. It knows which app has the microphone, and a muted meeting still counts.
  • Two rhythms, never back to back — Nothing lands within ten minutes of a break ending, and a move break rests your eyes too.
  • A heads-up first — A card a minute ahead with Start now, +1, +5 and +15, then a five-second countdown by the cursor.
  • A calmer break screen — Your desktop blurs behind one instruction, a draining ring and the countdown. Escape twice skips.
  • Guided breaks — A dot to follow for near and far, paced blinking, a breathing circle, stepped stretches.
  • Planned breaks — Lunch, a walk, anything at a fixed time.
  • Presets and quick timers — Balanced, Deep focus, Eye care, Wellness, and one-tap choices for both rhythms.
  • Skipping on your terms — Casual, Balanced or Hardcore, a daily snooze budget, and End break once three quarters are done.
  • Posture and blink reminders — Quiet nudges between breaks, off until you want them.
  • Make it yours — Backgrounds, your own words, chimes, automations, Shortcuts actions and two global hotkeys.
  • Your day, honestly — Screen time, stretches, top apps, a screen score, the week, and a Friday summary.
  • A rhythm coach — After a fortnight, one suggested change from how you actually break.
  • Time away counts — Vista says when it counted a break for you, and lets you take it back.
  • A new first run — The welcome tour, reopenable from General.
  • A warmer look — Warm ink, one accent, hairline rules, and settings in one sidebar window.
